extraction.name: BoolQ
extraction.description: BoolQ (Boolean Questions) is a reading comprehension dataset of 16,000 naturally occurring yes/no questions, each paired with a Wikipedia paragraph containing the answer. The questions are generated in unprompted and unconstrained settings, often querying complex, non-factoid information requiring difficult entailment-like inference.
extraction.creator: Christopher Clark, Kenton Lee, Ming-Wei Chang, Tom Kwiatkowski, Michael Collins, Kristina Toutanova
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions are gathered from anonymized, aggregated queries to the Google search engine. Queries likely to be yes/no questions are heuristically identified by selecting queries where the first word is in a manually constructed set of indicator words and are of sufficient length. Questions are only kept if a Wikipedia page is returned as one of the first five results. Human annotators then label question/article pairs in a three-step process: deciding if the question is good, finding a passage within the document that contains enough information to answer the question, and marking whether the answer is 'yes' or 'no'. The pipeline follows the Natural Questions (NQ) method with an additional filtering step to focus on yes/no questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Annotators can mark questions as 'not answerable' if the Wikipedia article does not contain the requested information.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Anonymized, aggregated queries to the Google search engine paired with Wikipedia pages returned as one of the first five search results.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three authors labelled 110 randomly chosen examples to assess annotation quality. Disagreements were resolved by mutual agreement among authors. The dataset uses singly-annotated examples in training/dev/test sets. An author also categorized 200 questions into topic types.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Answer annotations reached 90% accuracy compared to gold-standard labels. Of disagreements, six were ambiguous/debatable cases and five were annotator errors.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 annotation per item (singly-annotated), except for 110 quality-check examples which received labels from 3 authors
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has a natural filtering effect where factoid questions are rare, and negation is rarely present in passages and questions, which may limit the diversity of question types covered.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and evaluation of yes/no reading comprehension and question answering models, including transfer learning and fine-tuning experiments.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset has been updated at least once since initial release, though no formal maintenance plan is described.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Combined 13k questions from the NQ pipeline with 3k yes/no questions from the NQ training set (total 16k), then split into 3.2k dev, 3.2k test, and 9.4k train sets, ensuring NQ questions are always in the train set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions filtered to yes/no type using heuristic indicator words and length thresholds; only kept if a Wikipedia page appeared in top 5 search results; annotators filtered for comprehensible, unambiguous, factual questions; questions paired with selected passage (not full document) to reduce ambiguity and limit input size; non-answerable questions excluded.
